Subject: Private deploy kickoff — initial checklist request

Jonas / team,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Per our internal kickoff, the infra and security teams asked for a concise acceptance checklist and the network diagram with the specific CIDR ranges you expect us to peer to. We also need a clear list of KMS/HSM integration steps, including required roles and a sample policy so we can line up our security review next week.

We're targeting a smoke test week of Oct 11 — can you confirm what's needed from our side by Oct 4? Attached is our current topology (rough) — happy to refine.

Thanks,
Alex Gomez
Director, Platform Engineering
Medicorp

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy kickoff — initial checklist request

Alex — appreciate the quick start. High level: we need three buckets from you by Oct 4 to make the Oct 11 smoke window realistic:

1) Network basics (by Oct 4)
  - Public egress IPs / CIDR ranges to be allowlisted (we'll provide our expected peer ranges).
  - BGP peering window: if you choose managed transit (preferred), share ASN and proposed BGP neighbors.
  - MTU for the private link (512/1500 mismatches are the most common gotcha).

2) Secrets & keys (by Oct 4)
  - KMS details (customer-managed KMS preferred). We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM via PKCS#11 for on-prem.
  - Required principal: a service account key for 'redwood-deploy-agent' with kms:Encrypt,Decrypt,GenerateDataKey permissions; we will hand over an example policy.

3) Accounts & access
  - Service accounts, list of engineers (SSH jumpbox access if on-prem), and audit contact.

I'll drop a technical checklist in the thread (from Karthik) and Ben will follow up on contract/procurement steps.

— Jonas
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: none
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@medicorp.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Technical checklist (detailed) — Medicorp private deployment

Alex / team — forwarding the technical checklist we run through during onboarding. I've kept items you can action in bold.

1) Network & routing  - Expected Redwood peer ranges: 10.240.200.0/24 (control plane), 10.241.0.0/16 (data plane). Please confirm there is no overlap with your tenant ranges.  - If using BGP: provide ASN, neighbor IPs, BGP password (if configured), and whether you expect route maps.  - Transit: do you plan to terminate on your existing transit (preferred) or hand us a cross-connect? If cross-connect, share ticket to your cloud provider port.  - Egress & NAT: confirm if outbound traffic must come from a fixed set of IPs (we can provide static egress IPs for the dedicated link).  - MTU: confirm 1500 vs 9001 for jumbo frames.

2) DNS & service discovery  - Internal DNS entries we will register: redis.private.medicorp, redis.ops.medicorp. Provide zone delegation if you want us to manage service names.

3) Secrets & KMS  - Preferred: Customer-managed KMS key (AWS/GCP). We'll request a key ARN and attach policy for 'kms:GenerateDataKey'.  - On-prem HSM: we support PKCS#11. **If HSM**, provide vendor, PN and a test partition + credentials.  - Bring your own key rotate window expectations (we recommend quarterly rotation).

4) Access & telemetry  - SIEM/Log forwarding: provide endpoint for syslog or a S3/GCS bucket for shipping audit logs.  - SSH jumpbox: public IP and allowed CIDRs if needed.

5) Validation & smoke tests (what Redwood will run)  - Control-plane handshake, model load, inference baseline (1k qps synthetic), end-to-end latency sample.  - Customer must confirm: sample inference payload, retention policy for logs, and acceptance SLO (p99 < 200ms).

6) Contingencies  - If we encounter KV cache warmup latency >2s, we will fail over to a quantized model variant automatically unless you request otherwise.

Action items for Medicorp by Oct 4: bolded items above (CIDRs, ASN, KMS details, access list).

I'll attach a formal checklist XLS and a suggested IAM policy.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-private-deploy-checklist.xlsx (attachment stub), sample-kms-policy.txt (attachment stub)

Thanks — quick clarifications from our security team:

- We plan to use our AWS KMS key (arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789:key/abcd-ef01). Can you confirm Redwood's exact actions so our IAM policy is scoped correctly?
- For the egress IPs: we need the definitive list of Redwood egress addresses to paste into our firewall rules. Can you provide those as static values for the dedicated link?
- On HSM: not required for now, but we may revisit after initial run.

Also if you have an acceptance checklist matrix that maps 'pass/fail' criteria to test scripts, that would help speed security sign-off.

— Jordan
Security Architect
Medicorp

- Acceptance matrix (CSV) mapping checks to test scripts and expected thresholds.
- A 45-minute smoke-test runbook (step-by-step) for Oct 11.

- Oct 11: Customer-facing smoke tests (2-hour window)

If that works we'll schedule the Friday network alignment call (30 minutes) — ping preferred times and we'll send calendar invites.

— Laura Bennett
